# German Idealism quotes

German Idealism develops post-Kantian systems in which freedom, self-consciousness, and historical reason are tightly linked.

15 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

After Kant’s critical turn, Fichte, Schelling, and Hegel (and related receptions) argue about the absolute, dialectic, and ethical life. Passages here emphasize freedom realized in thought and institutions.

## Historical notes

Late eighteenth- and early nineteenth-century German philosophy sets agendas for Marxism, existentialism, pragmatism, and contemporary continental thought.

## Core ideas

-   Freedom is not only private choice but realized form.
-   Self-consciousness develops through relation and recognition.
-   System and history can be thought together.
-   Critique of knowledge opens metaphysics rather than ending it.

[G. W. F. ## FAQ

### What is German Idealism?

It is the post-Kantian movement treating mind, freedom, and reality as systematically interrelated—often via dialectic.

### Is Kant a German Idealist?

Kant is the decisive precursor; ‘German Idealism’ usually names the generation that radicalized his insights.
